extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and LaTeX users preparing commutative diagrams and AMS-LaTeX documents (users of xypic/xy-matrix, graphics inclusion, macros, lists, and bibliographies)
extracted.subtask_short: creating XY-pic commutative diagrams in LaTeX
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and best practices for constructing commutative diagrams with XY-pic (xymatrix) and related LaTeX document tasks (including graphics, macros, lists, and bibliographies) targeted at authors preparing mathematical documents with AMS-LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifying a hole in a crossing arrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the !{[u];[r]}{\hole} syntax to place a hole where one arrow crosses another, indicating the relative nodes used to compute the crossing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: !{[u];[r]}{\hole} because the arrow with the hole begins at D and, relative to that node, the arrow that crosses over goes from the node [u] to the node [r].

rubrics_metrics.name: Making room for large labels
rubrics_metrics.description: If arrow labels are large and overwrite nodes, either enlarge the entire diagram or create an empty row/column for arrows to span so labels have space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: enlarge entire diagram using spacing commands (see 8.7.1), or create a row/column whose nodes are empty and have arrows span them (see 8.7.2). You can also insert an \hspace into an empty node to add extra room; no need to add it on every row.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarging the entire diagram with spacing commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Use xymatrix spacing options (e.g., @C=6em) to enlarge the diagram grid so labels have room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \xymatrix@C=6em{ ... } enlarges column spacing. Use the spacing commands described in section 8.2; use em for horizontal measures to scale with font.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating an empty column/row to increase label space
rubrics_metrics.description: Add an extra column (or row) whose nodes are empty and use multi-step arrow commands (e.g., \ar[rr]) so labels sit over/around the empty space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: create four columns with the second column empty and use \ar[rr] for the labeled arrows. To increase more space, put an \hspace command into one of the empty nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow style selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose arrow styles using \ar@{...} notation to produce dotted, dashed, multiple-heads, tails, or other arrow types; you can also omit head/tail or the arrow shaft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 lists many forms: \ar@{.>}, \ar@{-->}, \ar@{=>}, \ar@{:>}, \ar@{->>}, \ar@{>->}, \ar@{<->}, \ar@{|->}, \ar@{^{(}->}, etc. Omit head/tail to place things outside the grid or use invisible arrows (\ar@{}) for positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using invisible arrows to place content (e.g., equals sign)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invisible arrow (\ar@{} ...) can be used to place symbols or text in the middle of a crossing (for example, to place an equals sign breaking the invisible arrow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \ar@{}[dr]|{=} inserts an equals sign by breaking the middle of the invisible arrow from the upper-left node to the lower-right node.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curved arrows: specifying default curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \ar@/^/ or \ar@/_/ after \ar to curve an arrow up or down by a default amount; labels can be added as usual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \ar@/^/[target], \ar@/_/[target] or with label \ar@/^/[target]^{label}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curved arrows: specifying the amount of curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify explicit curvature magnitude by giving a dimension after the ^ or _: \ar@/^1ex/[target] (or any unit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: measure vertical distances in ex and horizontal in em so dimensions scale with font. Units: in, cm, pt, em, ex, etc. Examples show \ar@/^3ex/ and \ar@/_3ex/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curved arrows: specifying start and end directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \ar@(start,end)[target] to control the direction from which an arrow leaves its source and the direction from which it approaches its target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \ar@(r,u)[dr]^{f} or \ar@(d,l)[dr]_{g}; start and end directions use compass letters (r, l, u, d, ur, ul, dr, dl).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sliding arrows sideways / multiple parallel arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: To have more than one straight arrow between the same pair of nodes, slide arrows up or down with \ar@<dimen> (positive moves 'upwards', negative moves 'downwards').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \ar@<1ex>[r] and \ar@<-1ex>[r] for parallel arrows. You can also slide curved arrows using combinations like \ar@/^1ex/@<1ex>[r]. Prefer ex for vertical spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifying both source and target of an arrow (relative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \ar[source];[target] to specify both ends of an arrow rather than assuming the current node is the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: \ar[target] is equivalent to \ar[];[target] because [] denotes the current node. This lets you list arrows separately from node definitions and save arrow descriptions 'until the end'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute specification of nodes by row and column
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify a node absolutely as "p,q" (including quotes), where p is row number and q is column number (rows count from top starting at 1; columns count from left starting at 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \ar^{f}"1,2" or \ar_{f} "1,1";"1,2" to specify arrows between absolute positions. Useful in combination with \ar(source);"p,q" syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nodes off the grid with \save and \restore
rubrics_metrics.description: Place nodes at arbitrary positions using \save ... \restore around displacement operations like []+<Dx,Dy>*+{stuff} and optionally name them for later reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within a save/restore excursion you can move using []+<Dx,Dy>, typeset with *+{...}, name nodes with *+{...}="name", and draw arrows to/from these nodes. Use ex/em for vertical/horizontal distances. Named off-grid nodes can be referenced later in absolute specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming nodes for later arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating an off-grid node you may name it, e.g., *+{H}="firstthing", so arrows can later be specified using the name "firstthing" as source or target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage: \save []+<4em,1em>*+{H}="firstthing" \restore then later \ar"firstthing";"1,2"_{p} etc. Semicolon separates source and target when specifying both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text objects in diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert text objects using *\txt{Some text} or *\txt<width>{Some text}. Use *+ or *++ to add surrounding space. Use *+[l] or *+[r] to shift alignment left or right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the first form you create linebreaks with \\; in the second, lines are broken automatically. By default arrows to/from text objects go to their center; shifting may be necessary to avoid overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows to/from points off nodes (arrows off the grid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify arrow endpoints at points other than nodes by adding a displacement vector +<Dx,Dy> to a node reference (e.g., \ar[d]+<4em,0ex> ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displacements use units (em, ex, pt, cm, in). You can specify both source and target with displacements, combine with curving, and label such arrows as usual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dropping objects/annotations at arbitrary diagram points
rubrics_metrics.description: Drop text or math at any point by drawing an arrow to that point and placing a text/math object at the arrow end (e.g., \ar[]+<5em,-5ex>*+\txt{...};[]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use invisible arrows (\ar@{}) to avoid printing the arrow. Default placement puts the center of the text at the specified point; shift (e.g., *+[r]) or increase displacement to avoid overlap. Example: \ar@{}[]+<8em,-4ex>*+\txt{Both $f$ and $g$\\are fibrations.}

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading graphics with graphicx
rubrics_metrics.description: Load the graphicx package via \usepackage{graphicx} when you need to include external graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: graphicx.sty is the modern package (vs older graphics.sty). Use \includegraphics{file} to insert graphics. Standard practice is to put graphics in a figure environment to allow floating, captions, and labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including graphics: figure environment and caption/label placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include graphics inside a figure environment, center them with \centering, add a \caption (below the graphic), and then a \label (after the caption) to refer to the figure with \ref.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the center environment (adds vertical space); prefer \centering. The \label must come after \caption because \caption creates the number the label references. You may also put \label inside \caption: \caption{...\label{fig:...}}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic format compatibility: EPS vs PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: Different LaTeX workflows require different graphics formats: traditional latex (producing DVI) requires EPS files; pdflatex (producing PDF) requires PDF graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some installations may alias latex to pdflatex; check. To include EPS when producing PDF you can run plain latex then dvipdf, or use epstopdf to convert EPS to PDF. See AMS FAQ for platform-specific notes (e.g., TEXShop).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer \newcommand / \renewcommand over \def for macros
rubrics_metrics.description: In LaTeX prefer \newcommand (and \renewcommand when overriding) rather than plain TeX \def because LaTeX checks for existing definitions and gives errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Syntax: 
ewcommand{
ame}[n]{definition} for n parameters. Example: 
ewcommand{	ensor}{\otimes}. To override an existing definition use enewcommand{	ensor}{...}. For parameterized macros: 
ewcommand{\pushout}[3]{#1\cup_{#2}#3}.

rubrics_metrics.name: List environments: itemize, enumerate, description
rubrics_metrics.description: Use itemize for bulleted lists, enumerate for numbered lists, and description when each \item has a label you wish to display at its start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate auto-manages nested numbering. Examples show how long items wrap to subsequent lines and how nested enumerate uses (a), (b), (c) labels. description requires an argument for each item (e.g., \item[key] ...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing enumerated items by number
rubrics_metrics.description: To reference an item in an enumerate list use \label on the \item and later refer to it with \ref.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \item \label{step:trans} Put the transmission into drive. Then later: You must complete steps \ref{step:trans} and \ref{step:brake} before beginning step~\ref{step:move}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use amsrefs for bibliographies
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommended way to create a bibliography in AMS-LaTeX is to use the amsrefs package, which preserves structured metadata and makes styling/numbering simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: simple typing, correct formatting and automatic numbering, style changes without retyping items, optional reuse as a database. amsrefs can interoperate with BibTeX via a special style if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading and structuring amsrefs bibliographies (bibdiv/biblist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Load amsrefs with \usepackage[lite]{amsrefs}. Begin bibliographies with \begin{bibdiv}\begin{biblist} and end with \end{biblist}\end{bibdiv}. The outer environment produces the heading and the inner environment produces the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can place material between \begin{bibdiv} and \begin{biblist} to appear between the heading and the list. Define each bibliography item with a \bib command (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and rules for the \bib command in amsrefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bibliography entry is given with \bib{ReferenceKey}{ReferenceType}{ comma separated list of keyword={value} statements } where ReferenceType is article, book, misc, report, or thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules include: keywords must be lower case; values must be enclosed in braces; author names must be in 'von Last, First, Jr.' form; multiple authors use separate author fields; title capitalization is preserved as-typed; date formats: {YYYY}, {YYYY-MM}, or {YYYY-MM-DD}. Lists of allowed simple, repeatable, and compound fields are provided (simple: address, booktitle, date, edition, eprint, etc.; repeatable: author, editor, translator, isbn, issn, review; compound: book, conference, contribution, partial, reprint, translation). See section 12.2 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining amsrefs-formatted \bib entries from MathSciNet
rubrics_metrics.description: You can copy a fully filled-out \bib command from MathSciNet by selecting the 'AMSRefs' format in the 'Select Alternative Format' pulldown on a review page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: find the review on MathSciNet, choose 'AMSRefs' from 'Select Alternative Format', copy the resulting \bib command and paste it into your LaTeX file.
